clue.text: Reeling, right off, Margaret's violin piece?

indicators.note: off says the letter for right is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: reeling means spinning round, turning
Peg is a pet form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: Margaret, staggering about, owns some part of a violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right off' takes R out of TURNING, leaving TUNING.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuning peg is the wooden knob on a violin's scroll that tightens a string, so it is a piece of the instrument.

clue.text: Wife gets in smack — result of knicker elastic being tweaked?

definitions.text: result of knicker elastic being tweaked?

indicators.note: gets in says the wife's letter enters the word for smack

parts.note: a smack is a taste or flavour, a tang

explanation.surface: A wife slaps someone, and somebody's knicker elastic gets pinged.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucking a stretched elastic band makes a vibrating sound, a resonant noise like a plucked string.

clue.text: Star's upset over cryptic clue's focus

indicators.note: in a down clue the reversed star sits over and around the scrambled word, enclosing it
upset in a down clue means the word for star is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: the sun is our star

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters of clue are mixed up

explanation.surface: A celebrity is annoyed at a crossword clue's main point.
explanation.walkthrough: SUN reversed is NUS, which goes round CLEU, the jumbled letters of 'clue'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the central core or focal point around which something gathers, a synonym for focus.

clue.text: Brad Pitt's second part secured by network backing

indicators.note: secured by says the letter from Pitt is held inside the reversed network
backing in a down clue means the word for network is read in reverse

parts.note: LAN is a local area network

indicators.note: second part picks out the second letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something about the actor Brad Pitt's second role, fixed by a TV network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brad' looks like the actor's first name but is the definition; LAN reversed is NAL, round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A brad is a small thin nail with a tiny head, so the word names a kind of fastener.

clue.text: No 1 left island town

parts.note: number one is a childish euphemism for urinating, to pee

explanation.surface: The top person has departed from a town on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Peel is a town on the Isle of Man; 'No 1' is nursery talk for a wee.
explanation.definitionFit: Peel is a harbour town on the west coast of the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Relative origin of universe bounded by morphing rectangle

indicators.note: bounded by says the single letter is enclosed by the rearranged letters
morphing means changing shape, so the letters of rectangle are rearranged
origin of takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A cosmology picture: the universe began inside a shape-shifting rectangle.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-uncle is a parent's uncle, a family relation two generations up.

clue.text: Toast US abolitionist

definitions.meaning: to toast bread is to make it go golden in colour, to cook it to that shade
John ... led the 1859 raid on Harpers Ferry to end slavery

explanation.definitionFit: Toasting turns bread a darker colour; John Brown was the anti-slavery American hanged after Harpers Ferry.

clue.text: Terminal break just about engages with satellite's charged particle

indicators.note: engages means holds or takes in, so the word for break encloses the satellite's letters

parts.note: to bust something is to break it

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ion is an atom or molecule carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A satellite briefly picks up a charged particle during a break in transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' looks like an adjective but is a noun, a terminus; 'about' shuffles the satellite's three letters before 'engages' puts them inside the break.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus station is a terminus where coach and bus routes start and end.

clue.text: Italian town that's too upset to contain diatribe

indicators.note: to contain says the shuffled letters go around the word for diatribe
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of too are rearranged

parts.note: a diatribe is a bitter tirade, a rant

explanation.surface: A town in Italy is so annoyed that it cannot hold back a tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the town's mood but scrambles 'too' to OTO, which then holds the tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: Otranto is a port town in Apulia, on the heel of the Italian peninsula.

clue.text: City, inexperienced, play defensively

parts.note: someone inexperienced is new to the job
in chess, to castle is a defensive move protecting the king

explanation.surface: A city side of novices adopts a defensive game.
explanation.walkthrough: Castling, a chess move, tucks the king away safely.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle upon Tyne is a large city in north-east England.

clue.text: Water brought up by this old mathematician's team

parts.note: Archimedes of Syracuse was the ancient Greek mathematician; the possessive gives an extra S
a crew is a team, as of rowers

explanation.surface: A dead mathematician's team hauled up some water.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive ARCHIMEDES'S runs on into CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: This device is a helical blade in a tube that lifts liquid uphill as it turns, an ancient pump.

clue.text: Potty Earl?

parts.note: potty pretends to mean mad but means in a teapot; the earl is the PM who gave his name to a blend of tea

explanation.walkthrough: Earl Grey was a British prime minister, and Earl Grey is a bergamot-flavoured tea brewed in a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: The second Earl, a prime minister, lends his title to a tea that ends up in a pot.

clue.text: Way to back popular king with a currency

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: back says the little word to is read in reverse

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A road leading back to a well-liked king with money.
explanation.definitionFit: The stotinka is a Bulgarian coin, the hundredth part of a lev, so it is a monetary unit.

clue.text: Rising to the surface and new: stifling to boot

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the combined letters wrap around the little word

parts.note: water welling up is rising to the surface

explanation.surface: Something surfacing, fresh and suffocating as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to boot' looks like the phrase meaning also, but 'boot' alone is the definition and 'to' is the piece being stifled.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellington is a waterproof rubber boot, named after the Duke.

clue.text: A sure indication drunk has to set out

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
must means has to

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk must venture outside, a clear sign of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A litmus test is a decisive single indicator, from the paper that shows acid or alkali.

clue.text: One who tips off Nai concerning a famous surgeon

parts.note: something that lists tips or leans to one side, so one who tips is a lister

indicators.note: off means wrong or not right, so the letters of Nai are rearranged

explanation.surface: An informer gives Nai a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips off' looks like a phrase meaning warns; 'tips' goes with 'One who' and 'off' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery, and the adjective describes things relating to him.

clue.text: Organ and wind backing that's associated with the Beatles

parts.note: the liver is a body organ

indicators.note: backing in a down clue means the word for wind is read in reverse

parts.note: to wind is to coil, making a loop

explanation.surface: A musical picture: an organ and wind instruments in support of the Beatles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' and 'wind' suggest instruments, fitting the Beatles, but give body organ and coil.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool is the city where the Beatles formed and played at the Cavern Club.

clue.text: Grumpy old person is tense before chaotic flight

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a rout is a disorderly retreat

explanation.surface: A cantankerous pensioner gets nervous ahead of a messy journey by air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel but means running away.
explanation.definitionFit: An old trout is a British idiom for a bad-tempered or fussy elderly person, usually a woman.

clue.text: Loud eruption of Oval, when century's bagged

indicators.note: bagged means captured, so the shuffled letters hold the century letter
an eruption throws things about, so the letters of Oval are rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: The crowd at the Oval roars when a batsman makes a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, where a century is a hundred runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Vocal means outspoken and noisy, voicing things loudly.

clue.text: Challenge something said against nurse

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
to nurse someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: Someone disputes what a nurse was told.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend can mean to dispute or argue against a statement, taking issue with a claim.

clue.text: Brooks sustained said city?

parts.note: Mel Brooks is the American comedy film director

indicators.note: said means the word for sustained is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: sustained means carried or endured, borne

explanation.surface: Brooks kept up talk about a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: a bourne is a brook, so 'Brooks' doubles as a hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Melbourne is the state capital of Victoria in Australia.

clue.text: Tailless warbler is ideological symbol

indicators.note: tailless means the bird's name loses its last letter

parts.note: a redstart is a songbird, loosely a warbler

explanation.surface: A bird with no tail stands for some ideology.
explanation.definitionFit: The red star is the emblem of communism, seen on Soviet flags and badges.

clue.text: Row a loch, which is most unpleasant

definitions.note: a noun phrase here: the thing or quality that is most unpleasant

parts.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers or taxis
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: Rowing on a Scottish lake proves a miserable experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests rowing a boat but is a line. Loch Ness is a lake in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Rankness is the quality of being rank, foul-smelling or offensive in the extreme.

clue.text: South West abandons country garden

indicators.note: abandons says the letters for south-west leave the country's name

parts.note: Sweden is a Scandinavian country
SW is the compass abbreviation for south-west

explanation.surface: Someone from the south-west quits the country for a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical garden of Adam and Eve.

clue.text: Russian Orthodox housing shown at the top of a map?

definitions.text: shown at the top of a map?

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the answer sits inside the run of the two words

explanation.surface: A Russian Orthodox church building marked at the top of a map.
explanation.definitionFit: Maps are conventionally drawn with this compass direction at the top edge.

clue.text: Round, bum-shaped tree of the South American pampas

definitions.text: tree of the South American pampas

parts.note: O is a round shape

indicators.note: shaped means formed anew, so the letters of bum are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree on the Argentine plains has a round, bottom-like form.
explanation.definitionFit: The ombu is a large evergreen of the Argentine and Uruguayan grasslands, a lone shade tree on the plains.

clue.text: Gull's call follows second diver

indicators.note: follows says the gull's cry comes after the letter for second

parts.note: a mew is the cry of a gull

explanation.surface: A gull cries just after another seabird plunges in.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small diving duck, a sawbill that hunts underwater.

clue.text: Kitchen aid's helium-filled retro movement adjusted

definitions.note: the possessive reads as kitchen aid is, linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so the pooled letters are rearranged

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget containing helium has had its backward mechanism tweaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filled' just says the HE goes in with the other letters before all fifteen are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven thermometer is a cooking gadget that measures heat inside the oven, a kitchen tool.

clue.text: City haunt of vice is taxed

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a den is a place of iniquity, as in den of thieves

explanation.surface: A city's den of iniquity pays its taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taxed' means loaded or burdened, not charged a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means heavily loaded, burdened, as taxed can mean strained by a load.

clue.text: Electronic bank withdrawal — in reality, it might not be fully reflected in the cost

definitions.text: it might not be fully reflected in the cost

indicators.note: in says the electronic letter and reversed bank sit inside the word for reality

parts.note: truth means reality, what is actually the case

indicators.note: withdrawal suggests drawing back, so the word for bank is read in reverse

parts.note: a bank of switches or oars is a row

explanation.surface: Taking cash from a bank by card is, in truth, a matter of value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank withdrawal' looks like taking out cash; here a bank is a line of things, drawn back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Real value can differ from the price paid, so a price may not fully reflect it.
